description: Implement full authentication flow using Supabase Auth (mocked for demo). This includes: a login page (/login) with email/password form, a signup page (/signup) with email/password registration, logout functionality, password reset flow with forgot-password and /reset-password pages, persistent session management via onAuthStateChange, a profiles table in Supabase with auto-creation trigger on signup, and an AuthContext provider that exposes user state throughout the app. New users default to the Requestor role. The auth system coexists with demo mode — when in demo mode, auth is bypassed entirely. When not in demo mode, unauthenticated users are redirected to /login from any /app/* route.

stories.title: Create AuthContext provider
stories.description: Create src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx with a React context providing: user (Supabase User | null), profile (Profile | null), isLoading (boolean), isAuthenticated (boolean), signIn(email, password), signUp(email, password), signOut(), resetPassword(email). For now, all auth methods are stubs that log to console — real Supabase integration comes when Cloud is enabled. Also create src/hooks/useAuth.ts convenience hook. The provider wraps the app in RootComponent alongside DemoProvider.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthContext provides user, profile, isLoading, isAuthenticated
signIn, signUp, signOut, resetPassword methods exist (stubbed)
useAuth hook returns context value with error if outside provider
Provider wraps app in RootComponent
isAuthenticated returns false when no user, true when user exists
isLoading starts true, becomes false after initial check
Both files under 150 lines each

verification.test: Open /. In React DevTools, find AuthProvider. Context should show user: null, isAuthenticated: false, isLoading: false. No console errors.

stories.title: Create login page
stories.description: Create src/routes/login.tsx at /login. Centered card layout with Stackwise wordmark, 'Sign in to your account' heading, email input, password input, 'Sign In' submit button (teal primary), 'Forgot password?' link below, and 'Don't have an account? Sign up' link at bottom. Form validates email format and non-empty password before submission. On submit, calls signIn from AuthContext. Shows toast on error. On success, navigates to /app/dashboard. If user is already authenticated, redirect to /app/dashboard. If in demo mode, also redirect to /app/dashboard.

stories.title: Route protection for /app/* routes
stories.description: Add route protection logic so that /app/* routes require either demo mode OR authentication. Create src/lib/auth-guard.ts or add logic to the app.tsx layout route. If not in demo mode and not authenticated, redirect to /login. If in demo mode, always allow access. Show a brief loading spinner while auth state is being determined (isLoading: true). The guard should not flash the login page before redirecting authenticated users.
acceptanceCriteria: Unauthenticated, non-demo users redirected from /app/* to /login

Authenticated users have access to /app/*
Loading spinner shown while auth state resolves
No flash of login page for authenticated users
Redirect preserves intended destination (optional, nice to have)

verification.test: Open /app/dashboard directly without demo or auth — should redirect to /login. Enter demo mode from landing page — should access /app/dashboard freely. Exit demo mode, try /app/dashboard again — should redirect to /login. No console errors.

stories.title: Auth form error handling and edge cases
stories.description: Ensure all auth forms (login, signup, forgot-password, reset-password) handle error states gracefully. Network errors show a toast with 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' Invalid credentials show inline error 'Invalid email or password.' Rate limiting shows 'Too many attempts. Please wait.' All error messages are user-friendly, not raw Supabase errors. Add a generic ErrorAlert component (src/components/ErrorAlert.tsx) for reuse across forms.
acceptanceCriteria: Login form shows 'Invalid email or password' on auth failure
Signup form shows specific errors (email taken, weak password)
Network error shows toast notification
All error messages are user-friendly, no raw error codes
ErrorAlert component created and used across auth forms
Error state clears when user starts typing again
ErrorAlert component under 40 lines

verification.test: Open /login. The form should render without errors. Since auth is stubbed, simulate an error by temporarily making signIn reject — error should display inline, not as raw error. Error should clear on input change. No console errors.
